questions.q: What does a dynamic data masking policy actually change about the underlying table when it's applied?
options: Nothing — the stored bytes stay exactly the same; only what a query returns changes
It permanently overwrites the sensitive columns with masked values
It deletes the sensitive columns entirely
It creates a second, permanently masked copy of the table
questions.explain: Dynamic masking is evaluated at query time. The table's stored data is untouched — Snowflake rewrites what a given query returns based on who's running it.

questions.q: In the lesson's example, what determines whether a query sees the real values or the masked values?
options: The time of day the query runs
CURRENT_ROLE() at the moment the query executes
Which warehouse size is in use
Whether the query uses a WHERE clause
questions.explain: The masking policy's CASE logic branches on CURRENT_ROLE() — a privileged role like ACCOUNTADMIN sees real values, everyone else sees the masked version.

questions.q: What happened when the same low-privileged role queried customer_loyalty_metrics_v, a downstream view built on the masked base table?
options: The view bypassed masking and showed real values
The view errored out because masking isn't supported on views
The view still returned masked values, with no extra configuration needed
The view returned blank columns instead of masked ones
questions.explain: Masking travels downstream automatically — a view built on a masked table is masked too, without being configured separately.

questions.q: How does dynamic masking differ from static (ETL-time) masking, per this lesson?
options: They're the same thing with different names
Static masking only works on numeric columns
Static masking permanently rewrites values (often into a separate lower-environment copy), while dynamic masking evaluates fresh at query time without altering storage
Dynamic masking requires a nightly batch job
questions.explain: Static masking is a one-time rewrite of the data, typically producing a masked copy for a lower environment. Dynamic masking never rewrites storage — it decides what to show at the moment each query runs.

questions.q: In the masked result shown, how was the e_mail column masked?
options: The entire address, including the domain, was replaced with MASKED
The local part before the @ was masked, but the real domain was kept
Only the top-level domain (.com) was masked
E-mail was not masked at all in the example
questions.explain: The masked e_mail values showed a masked local part concatenated with the real domain, e.g. **~MASKED~**@gmail.com.
